channel.title: Desert Garden Guide
channel.description: Practical wisdom for cacti, native plants, and water-wise gardens in arid climates — without fighting the land.

item.title: How to Plant a Desert Bird Garden
item.description: Attract Gambel's quail, mourning doves, curve-billed thrashers, and migrating songbirds by planting native desert shrubs, trees, and grasses that provide food, cover, and nesting habitat.

item.title: How to Grow Chiltepin Pepper in the Desert
item.description: The chiltepin is the only native wild chili pepper of the United States—fiercely hot, wildly aromatic, and surprisingly rewarding once you understand its Sonoran Desert roots. Learn how to grow this heritage crop at home.

item.title: The Best Desert Plants for Poolside Landscaping
item.description: The right plants around a desert pool handle reflected heat, chlorine splash, and minimal water — while keeping the skimmer clean. Here's what actually thrives in a Sonoran or Mojave poolscape.

item.title: Desert-Friendly Roses: Best Varieties for Extreme Heat and Drought
item.description: Most hybrid tea roses were never designed for 110°F summers and alkaline desert soil. But Knock Out shrubs, ancient Damask varieties, and tough China roses thrive where others fail. Here's how to choose, plant, and care for roses that actually perform in the desert.

item.title: How to Care for Desert Plants During Monsoon Season
item.description: Monsoon storms deliver half the Sonoran Desert's annual rainfall in intense afternoon bursts — and can rot established cacti, flood succulents, and trigger explosive weed growth overnight. Here's how to prepare, protect, and make the most of the desert's most dramatic season.

item.title: How to Grow Desert Wolfberry: The Southwest's Native Superfood Shrub
item.description: Desert wolfberry (Lycium fremontii) produces edible red berries, hosts nesting birds, feeds over 40 bird species, and thrives on almost no water once established in the Sonoran or Chihuahuan Desert. Here's how to plant, water, harvest, and maintain this underrated Southwest native shrub.

item.title: Composting in the Desert: Challenges and Solutions
item.description: Composting in arid climates presents unique challenges — extreme heat, low humidity, and alkaline soil conspire against traditional bin methods. Here's how to produce rich, dark humus that transforms desert soil using hot composting, worm bins, trench composting, and bokashi.

item.title: How to Grow Desert Spoon (Dasylirion) in Your Yard
item.description: Desert spoon (Dasylirion wheeleri) is one of the most architecturally dramatic plants in the Southwest — a bold sphere of blue-green, serrated leaves that thrives on almost no water, tolerates hard freezes, and looks spectacular year-round. Here's how to site, plant, water, and maintain this iconic Chihuahuan Desert native.

item.title: How to Grow Blackfoot Daisy in the Desert
item.description: Blackfoot daisy (Melampodium leucanthum) blooms nonstop for nine months a year on almost no water, tolerates 110°F afternoons, and thrives in the alkaline caliche soil that kills most perennials. Here's how to site, plant, water, and get years of white flowers from this tough Chihuahuan Desert native.

item.title: How to Start Desert Plants from Seed: A Complete Guide
item.description: Starting cacti, succulents, and native wildflowers from seed gives you access to hundreds of varieties unavailable at local nurseries. Here's exactly how to germinate and raise desert plants in arid climates — from timing and soil mix to watering and transplanting.

item.title: How to Grow Milkweed for Monarchs in the Desert
item.description: Several desert-native milkweed species thrive in Sonoran and Chihuahuan heat with almost no water — and every plant you grow is a lifeline for the endangered Western monarch population. Here's how to choose the right species and avoid the tropical milkweed trap.

item.title: How to Grow Lantana in the Desert: Brilliant Color Through Summer Heat
item.description: While other flowering plants wilt in 110°F heat, lantana hits its stride — blooming nonstop from spring through the first frost, drawing butterflies by the dozen, and thriving on almost no water once established. Here's how to pick the right cultivar and grow it well.

item.title: How to Grow Senna in the Desert: A Guide to Cassia Species
item.description: Senna shrubs light up desert yards with cascades of vivid yellow blooms for months — fixing nitrogen, hosting specialist native bees, and feeding quail — all with almost no supplemental water. Here's how to choose the right species and grow it well.

item.title: How to Grow Autumn Sage in the Desert: A Complete Salvia greggii Guide
item.description: Salvia greggii blooms red, pink, and coral from spring through fall in Chihuahuan and Sonoran Desert heat — and feeds hummingbirds for months with almost no supplemental water. Here's how to plant, prune, and choose the right cultivar.

item.title: How to Grow Agastache (Hummingbird Mint) in the Desert
item.description: Desert-native agastache species — sunset hyssop, Texas hummingbird mint, and orange agastache — bloom from midsummer through fall in 110°F heat, thrive in alkaline soil, and draw hummingbirds, bumblebees, and monarch butterflies with almost no supplemental water.

item.title: How to Grow Globe Mallow in the Desert
item.description: Globe mallow (Sphaeralcea) erupts in vivid orange, pink, and lavender blooms across the Sonoran and Mojave deserts with almost no supplemental water. It also hosts specialist native bees that depend on it for survival — making it one of the highest-value native wildflowers you can plant.

item.title: The Best Desert Plants for Erosion Control on Slopes
item.description: Monsoon rains erode bare desert slopes fast. These deep-rooted natives — sideoats grama, deer grass, Apache plume, brittlebush, creosote, and more — anchor soil, survive drought, and establish with almost no supplemental water.

item.title: How to Grow Fairy Duster (Calliandra) in the Desert
item.description: Calliandra eriophylla erupts in pink pom-pom blooms from late winter through monsoon season, attracts hummingbirds and butterflies, and thrives on almost no supplemental water. Here's the complete guide to growing this Sonoran Desert native.

item.title: How to Grow Dragon Fruit in the Desert
item.description: Dragon fruit is a climbing cactus that thrives on Sonoran Desert heat, alkaline soil, and deep infrequent watering. Here's how to choose the right cultivar, build a support structure, and harvest 20–40 pounds per season.
